summary: Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones and return the weight of the last remaining stone (or 0).
mainInsight: Each step needs the two largest elements and then possibly inserts a new one - exactly the operations of a max-heap. Python's heapq is a min-heap, so store negated weights.

approaches.name: Sort every round
approaches.summary: Sort the list each time and pick the last two.

approaches.name: Max-heap (negated min-heap)
approaches.summary: Pop two largest, push the difference if non-zero.

promptVariants: Which structure repeatedly gives the two largest elements efficiently?
What pattern fits 'repeatedly take the max and reinsert'?
cards.explanation: Each extraction and insertion is O(log n). (Max-heap: priority queue)

promptVariants: Why do you store negative weights in Python's heapq?
cards.answer: heapq implements a min-heap; negating the values makes the smallest negative number correspond to the largest weight, so heappop returns the heaviest stone.
cards.explanation: Alternative: store (-weight) tuples or write a custom comparator.

promptVariants: Each of up to n rounds does O(log n) heap work, giving ___.
cards.explanation: Heapify O(n) plus up to n rounds of O(log n) pops/pushes.

promptVariants: What extra space does the heap approach use?
Can it be done in place?
cards.answer: O(n) for the negated list (or O(1) extra if you heapify the input list in place after negating). The sort-based approach is O(1) extra but slower.

promptVariants: Why `continue` when a == b and why push `-abs(a - b)`?
How do you get the final answer?
cards.code:
while len(heap) > 1:
    a = heapq.heappop(heap)
    b = heapq.heappop(heap)
    if a == b:
        continue
    heapq.heappush(heap, -abs(a - b))
return 0 if not heap else -heap[0]
cards.answer: Equal stones destroy each other, so nothing is pushed. Otherwise the remainder has weight |a - b| (a and b are negated, so abs gives the positive difference) and is pushed back negated. When the loop ends at most one stone remains: its weight is -heap[0], or 0 if none.
cards.explanation: The answer is the last stone's weight.

promptVariants: What happens when all stones cancel?
cards.explanation: The stones are equal and destroy each other, leaving no stones.

incorrectOptionExplanations.2: Equal stones do not leave a remainder.
